items.a: Yes. The core features are free. Premium is monthly, yearly or a one-time Lifetime purchase, and subscriptions start with a free week.

items.q: Does Spendry connect to my bank?
items.a: No. It never asks for a bank login. You add entries yourself, or import them from bank messages and Shortcuts automations.
On your iPhone and in your own iCloud account. Your records are never sent to Spendry's servers, so we can't see them.

items.q: How does the debt payoff plan work?
items.a: Add your debts with their balances and rates. Spendry orders them with the snowball or avalanche method, adds what you can pay on top each month and shows the month you'll be debt-free.

items.q: Can I share a budget with my partner or family?
items.a: Yes. Shared budgets and goals sync through iCloud, and everyone uses their own Apple Account.

items.q: Which devices does it work on?
items.a: iPhone and iPad with iOS 17 or later, with widgets, Siri and Shortcuts.

items.q: Which languages and currencies does it support?
items.a: 44 languages and every major currency. Investments and foreign currency accounts can keep their own currency.

debt_tool.title: Debt Payoff Calculator: Snowball vs Avalanche
debt_tool.description: Free debt payoff calculator: compare the snowball and avalanche methods and see the month you'll be debt-free and the interest you'll pay. No sign-up.
debt_tool.lead: Enter your debts and what you can pay on top of the minimums each month. See your debt-free month and total interest with the snowball and avalanche methods side by side.
debt_tool.name: Debt
debt_tool.extra: Extra you can pay each month
debt_tool.same: Both methods give the same result with these numbers.
debt_tool.stuck: These payments never clear the debt: they don't cover the interest. Raise the extra payment.
debt_tool.note: Sample debts; replace them with yours. Rates are treated as fixed, fees are not included.
prose: With the snowball method you pay off the smallest balance first. The first debt disappears quickly and its payment rolls into the next one, which keeps motivation high. With the avalanche method you pay off the highest interest rate first, which usually costs less interest overall, though the first payoff can take longer.

Every month each debt gets its minimum payment. The extra goes to the next debt in line, and a cleared debt's payment rolls over to the next. Both methods use the same monthly budget, so the difference you see is only the order.
Keep the plan up to date
Balances change every month. Spendry tracks your cards, loans and bills, keeps your snowball or avalanche plan current and reminds you before each payment is due.
debt_tool.extra_hint: Money you can put toward your debts on top of the minimum payments. The more you add, the sooner you are debt-free.

budget_tool.title: Monthly Budget Calculator: Needs, Wants and Savings
budget_tool.description: Free monthly budget calculator: split your take-home pay into needs, wants, and savings or debt payments in seconds. No sign-up.
budget_tool.lead: Enter your monthly take-home pay. Half goes to needs, thirty percent to wants and twenty percent to savings and paying off debt.
prose: It's a simple way to start a budget. Fifty percent of what you take home covers the things you must pay, thirty percent the things you choose, and twenty percent goes to savings and paying down debt.
If rent alone takes half of your income, the rule is a starting point, not a verdict. Move the split to fit your life, and pay off high-interest debt first.
In Spendry each category gets a monthly budget that fills as you spend, with a warning before you go over.
